blocks.content: CVC exercises superintendence over the functioning of the CBI in so far as it relates to the investigation of offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act.

rows: Non-Statutory Body (Derives power from DSPE Act, 1946)
Vigilance, advisory, and supervisory body for central government integrity
Premier criminal investigative agency for corruption, economic offenses, and conventional crimes
Independent body reporting directly to the Parliament
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions (DoPT)

items: CBI is NOT a statutory body; it derives its investigative powers from the Delhi Special Police Establishment (DSPE) Act, 1946.
CVC was converted into a statutory body by an Act of Parliament in 2003 based on the Santhanam Committee recommendations.
The Director of CBI is appointed by a committee consisting of the Prime Minister (Chairperson), Leader of Opposition/Largest Opposition Party, and Chief Justice of India (or a nominated SC Judge).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: CVC is an apex vigilance advisory body established in 1964 and granted statutory status in 2003.
CBI is the premier investigating agency of India, established in 1963 by an executive resolution of the Ministry of Home Affairs.
CVC is a statutory body, whereas CBI is a non-statutory body deriving its powers from the Delhi Special Police Establishment (DSPE) Act, 1946.
CVC exercises superintendence over the functioning of CBI in matters relating to the investigation of offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
Both agencies were set up based on the recommendations of the Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption (1962–1964).
